Closure of Hyderabad and Bangalore Airports  
SHRI D. RAJA (Tamil Nadu): Sir, thank you for this opportunity. Morning, I tried to raise this issue. I draw the 
attention of the House and the Government to the si tuation that is arising out of the countrywide agit ation by the 
Airport Employees in all the airports of the countr y opposing and protesting the scandalous decision o f the 
Government to close down the Airports Authority of India airports at Hyderabad and Bangalore to allow the private 
sector airports coming up in these two major cities.  
Sir, the closure decision is the outcome of the infamous agreement entered into by the Government of India and 
the private airport companies in Hyderabad and Bang alore and this scandalous act was finally committed  in July, 
2004. During the last years, the air traffic in these two cities has gone up manifold and the decision of closure of the 
existing airports is against the public interest only to allow monopoly gains to private operators.  

192   Matters Raised  [RAJYASABHA]  with Permission  
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport and Tourism, in its report submitted in this very House on 
5th March, 2008, unanimously recommended not to close down these airports and renegotiate the agreement, but the 
Government is going ahead with the closure decision and the Hyderabad Airport is going to be closed down on the 
14th March. ESMA has been inflicted on the agitating employees who are fighting for their right cause. The act of 
the Government is also an insult to the Parliament. 
I urge upon the Chair to direct the Government to give credence to the Standing Committee report and defer the 
closure of airports and re-examine the whole matter . I urge upon the Government not to confront the ag itating 
employees and discuss with their joint forum which has been leading the agitation, while putting off  the decision to 
close the airports. I really urge upon the Governme nt, irrespective of the political parties, to consi der the issue, 
(Interruptions).  
SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT (West Bengal): Sir, we all associate.  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Yes, the whole House associates with the issue. (Interruptions).  
Shri Shahid Siddique; he is not here.

DR. M.S. GILL (Punjab): Sir, I welcome the Railway Budget. I support a lot of the things that have been done in 
it. There is no doubt that it has broad acceptance. Fares have been kept down; they are brought down every year. 
The number of trains has been increased. Broad gaug e lines have been added and some new lines have also been 
added. Freight work has been expanded. And there are a whole lot of other ideas which one would welcome. I am very 
interested in container traffic, bulk-handling arra ngements and door-to-door logistical arrangements. All these 
would help the Railways. It is our greatest public enterprise and we welcome whatever good has been achieved in it. 
But I have to say one thing here. Looking over the past, it is my impression that for a long period the Railways have 
not been able to have the amount of new investment which they need essentially. If one looks back over the past 
years, in every Budget, since there is a democratic constraint not to load the traveller, the resources are limited. A 
few new lines and a few new other things are announ ced. Sometimes they get done and sometimes they do not 
get done. The result is that this vast sub-continen t has not done much addition to the British railways. In my eyes, 
this is not what we could have done. I would have by now, in 60 years, seen the Indian Railway track doubled. I now 
hear this entire House and people say this; Chhattisgarh is not getting new trains.  

Matters Raised  [12 MARCH 2008]  with Permission    197  
Himachal Pradesh and Punjab have not got that tiny little 20 kilometres track to Una from Hoshiarpur s o as to 
provide the hill men a little connectivity. North E ast has really got nothing while China has come to Tibet; they 
are coming to the Chumbi Valley and to the Sikkim b order, and it should concern us. These are matters of big 
implications. Therefore, basically, the investment, as in agriculture, has not been enough for ten-fifteen years in the 
Railways, and in my eyes, it has not been what India could have had. The result is that we fight over small things.  
(THE VICE-CHAIRMAN, PROF. P.J. KURIEN in the Chair) 
My friend the last speaker has listed trains or has listed new tracks and they all, obviously, have a heavy bias 
towards one State. I would also list certain things. Punjab, in the last 60 years, has not really got anything in new 
tracks. It is a matter of record. No new tracks have been built, I shall give you one example. We are not linked to our 
capital, Chandigarh, It is an amazing thing. First, we have to share the capital between Punjab and Ha ryana and 
then, we are not linked to it. In Punjab there must  be links from Jalandhar and Ludhiana to Chandigarh . 
Chandigarh-Ludhiana is the richest area in India for agriculture and industry. It would earn the highest income to 
the Railways and to the country. But it is not link ed. Twenty miles have been built; the 30 miles to Ludhiana are 
still not built. It does not help the country, forget about Punjab. This is the story all over. Of the four small trains that 
we had hoped for, there is no mention or there is some vague mention. I am interested in one mention made in the 
Budget and that is Public-Private Partnership for w hich Rs. 1,00,000 crore are sought in the coming years. Well, 
four years of Parliament and of the Government have gone. I wonder whether they will get it in their last year. I wish 
it had been thought of earlier. But I do welcome it.  
If we can build a super highway—Gujarat has got it and other parts of India are getting it—and pay tol l tax, I 
don't see why some such arrangements, which are there in the West, cannot be made here for new trains for which 
investment will be made from outside Government. People will get trains and pay for them. The freight will pay for 
it. I welcome that. But, unless we do that, frankly , we are really stuck at the same level whatever we  claim our 
success to be. The entire infrastructure needs to be upgraded. There are basic things like bridges. You get five or ten 
thousand bridges in India. Half worth demolishing; they are hundred years old and many fall down on trains and 
you have regular accidents. The tracks have to be upgraded. Forget about the french trains. We can all have a train 
with a speed of 140-150 kmph. We will be able to do  more overnight, but that means reupgrading the track and 
improving it. The signal system is archaic and that leads to accidents.  
I read the accident figures here. There is an improvement. From 234 in 2005-06, to 195 in 2007. So, there are 
about 30-40 less accidents. But the point is: Why s hould there be almost 200 accidents in India? Why? Nobody 
else has it whether it is France, Germany or Spain. The technology is there, but we need a new signalling system in 
the whole country and that again needs investment.  
Now I come to rolling stock. I read what is being done and I welcome it. Rolling stocks including new coaches 
need huge money. Freight corridor is, I think, a brilliant idea—from Ludhiana up to Kolkata and from Delhi down to 
Mumbai. But when will it get done? Where will the money for investment come from?  
Members are asking and even I think that while the label will remain, we will spend our lifetime waiting for it. 
Incidentally, what is the logic of freight corridor from Kolkata going

only up to Ludhiana in the middle of the Punjab? It has to logically go to Atari border, so that we can trade with 
Pakistan also. We are going to trade and we are tra ding. Therefore, you are going to need something wh ere 
straightaway Pakistan container traffic is loaded a nd goes to Kolkata and Mumbai. So, please extend it  there. 
Please build it, to attach border. It is our dream that trains will go through Pakistan, Afghanistan, Turkmenistan all 
the way to Paris, Moscow and London. We are building the corridors down to Bangkok through Burma. This is the 
massive link of the new world of the 21 st Century.  So, please don't leave it up to Ludhiana. Please b uild it to 
Pakistan border.  
Therefore, I want to emphasise that for infrastructure requirement we need huge money. You will have to find it 
and I think methods are exist. We have new ports al ong the Gujarat coast and elsewhere. A lost of priv ate 
companies have opened up suddenly new ports. Otherw ise, people like me saw only Kandla, which is very good. 
The port wast built by the Government of India. So,  I think, this is an important one and without upgr ading the 
entire infrastructure, I am afraid, accidents and every other wrong will happen. I have to talk, since I am an MP, of 
new trains and a little bit of Punjab. As I said, please complete the Murinda corridor, 30 miles to Ludhiana, so that 
you get the Chandigarh-Ludhiana-Jalandhar-Amritsar link. You will earn and we will benefit and the country will 
benefit. Punjab in this Budget has been given, last year was also given, the Garib Rath from Amritsar to Saharsa. 
The Prime Minister went to Amritsar to inaugurate it. All of us were made to believe that it is a great gift to Punjab 
and I think the Prime Minister also did not realise that this hardly was a gift to Punjab. I have been checking Saharsa 
with my Bihar friends. It is in the middle of Bihar , perhaps next to Madhepura. No Punjabi wants to go  to 
Saharsa. I have no business there. But I know that there are a lot of people who come from Saharsa there, about 
forty lakhs of people come to Punjab. In Punjab, ou r house is open to everybody and it has always been , but 
surely, if they are going to benefit, it is really a train from Sarsa to Punjab. Then, a second train has been given, 
which is an express train, again from Amritsar to Sarsa. Now, I have been requesting, but I have not been heard, that 
these trains should end up in Kolkata so that the o dd Punjabi businessman from Amrtisar, the odd Punjabi Sikh, 
who is a truck driver in Kolkata, can go there. Otherwise, it does not mean anything for Punjab. I have to say that 
we don't have any new track or any new train. Himachal Pradesh does not have any. I think all these ne ed to be 
looked at and we must look at these things in a lar ger context. If I go back to my Election Commission  days, 
sometimes, I think like electoral constituencies, even the Ministries should be rotated among the Stat es. When we 
are sitting here, when I was in the Commission, and Laluji—I admire him much—is sitting here and other  Ministers 
are sitting in their Ministries, they are the Ministers, in my eyes, for India. Yes, there is a democratic requirement 
and slight biases are there. But, there has to be reasonable sharing for all of us somewhere in all these things.  
There is an important connection. I just want to put it on record. Really, I do not know when it will be looked 
at. Amritsar to Parti is an old British line. From Patti across the river, if you connect to Ferozepur , Ferozepur 
connects directly to Gujarat, Bombay and beyond. You get a parallel line; you get a Defence line; and, you get an 
economic line for industry, trade, everything, There will be, again, another parallel line coming from Bombay and 
going through Amritsar on to Pakistan and beyond. I would request that this should be looked at both as a security 
line—I as well as an economic line. I hope the hon. Minister will give it reasonable consideration.  
Then, there is the question of jobs. The Railways a re basically for jobs. That is why everybody wants this 
Ministry. I understand Railways  is a huge employer and there are

always more jobs. In this Budget also, I see about 7000 policemen, constables and then, of course, gangman, etc. 
Now, one thing I want to say, as an administrator, with some experience in this business, is that in a sub-continent, 
please, do not, in any Ministry, centralise all jobs of this country from gangman to paani-pilanewala at Delhi, and 
then, say that this is to get the best possible recruitment. No, Sir. We have got Railway Zones, or in other Ministries, 
we have similar structures. If the Northern Railway s want Class-IV chaprasis or gangkeepers, they should be 
recruited locally by North Zone out of those three-four States. They may not take a person from Punjab, but they may 
take person from Himachal or Rajasthan. The same policy should be followed in Bangalore or anywhere else. I believe 
it is necessary to consider this aspect. Otherwise, the Railways will give rise to intense dissatisfaction, of which we are 
all aware.  
Incidentally, there is a celebration of Guru Granth Sahib to be held at Nanded in Maharashtra. Now, there is a 
mention here that for 1 -3-4 days, on which they ce lebrate, there will be a train from Anandpur Sahib near 
Chandigarh and there will be a train from Patna. First of all, that does not link Punjab. Punjab train has to be from 
Amritsar, through the heart of the Punjab, to Nanded. A train from Patna to Nanded is also welcome because Guru 
Gobind Singh was born there. But, how many Sikhs or  people of this faith are living there. There are c ertainly 
some people.I would certainly say that first, from all over India, give them a train for those two-three days. But, 
second, I am not impressed even with what the Railw ays have given, that is, a train for three or four days. Some 
people may go and some people may not go on these days. After that, there is nothing. I would request the hon. 
Minister to link Amritsar with Nanded and Patna—we call Patna as 'Patna Saheb' because Guru Gobind Singh was 
born there—and link these various cities so that th ey can keep on going to their pilgrimages like we g o to many 
other pilgrim cities.  
I have already spoken about these new lines. Of cou rse, there is none for us. But, 150 kilometres are 
supposed to have been done in this year. For the ne xt year, it is 350 kilometres. It is a pittance. We  should be 
doing 1000 kilometres a year, at least. Then, the hon. Minister will satisfy most of these people.  
One thing I would say for my friend from Goa, becau se I have a relationship with them, that the Konkan  
railway is a good idea. It should be doubled because it is a major North-South line and needs doubling. Finally, the 
Kashmir line should be completed quickly. Thank you, Sir.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN): Ms. Anusuiya Uikey. Please remember that your Party has 
already exhausted the allotted time. Therefore, take only five minutes.

DR. K. MALAISAMY (Tamil Nadu): I thank you, Mr. Vic e-Chairman, Sir, for having spared a few minutes and 
permitting me to speak on the subject and supplement my colleagues who spoke on the same subject. Sir, last time 
when I was speaking on the Supplementary Budget on Railways, I made a comment that Laluji and Veluji 
combination has been working well. With the practical wisdom of Laluji-Laluji is not here —and the bur eaucratic 
background and experience of Veluji, it has been working very well. At that time also, I said this. Sir, I continue to 
hold the same opinion, but I would like to tell this House that I am neither there nor here, but in-between, to make 
some objective comments on them. In fact, on the UP A Government side, they have been highlighting what has 
been mentioned in the Budget. On the other side, it has been criticised. As far as I am concerned, I would like to 
make some objective comments, as to what can be done and what is wrong basically.  
Coming to, first and foremost, the introduction of high speed trains, in the Budget it has been said that high-speed 
trains are going to come. Okay. Quite welcome. I am very happy to hear that from Chennai to Coimbatore , from 
Chennai to Bangalore and from Chennai to Madurai, t hey are going to introduce high-speed trains. But the point 
is that we have come  

204   Matters Raised  [RAJYA SABHA]  with Permission  
across high speed trains in foreign countries where the maximum speed is somewhere around 200 kms. per hour. In 
India, the great Rajdhani Express or the Shatabadi Express can go up to 130-140 kms. per hour only. If that be the 
case, I would like to know whether they can afford to run, in Indian conditions, trains at 300 kms. per hour. It is a 
scheme which cannot be implemented. I want to know whether it is practical to run such trains. The hig h-speed 
trains introduction is most welcome. But, in Indian conditions, particularly, for high-speed trains, you should not 
have more number of level crossings. As far as Chennai to Coimbatore railway line is concerned, as many as 250 level 
crossings are there. Then, there should not be any sharp curve. In the high-speed trains, one should b e able to 
automatically put brakes if the driver fails. These are the conditions which are necessary for running  high-speed 
trains which are in existence in foreign countries. Are you fit enough to do all these things? That is my first point. 
Sir, I am very happy to know about the introduction of high-speed trains. According to me, it is impractical. The 
Minister may kindly clarify this point.  
Secondly, I come to the slow growth of the railway network. The Vice-Chairman, who is sitting there, is well-
informed. Sir, as far as the Railway network is concerned, during the year 1950-51 the total kilometre length was 
53,596 kilometres whereas, even after 50 years, in 2006-07, the total kilometre coverage is about 63,3 27 
kilometres. So, hardly 10,000 kilometres have been added during all these years. This is the growth of  railway 
network! That is my second point. You make tall cla ims about the growth, development etcetera. But ove r a 
period of 60 years, you are able to grow only 10,000 kilometres! That is a slow growth. It is very distressing to note 
that the rate of network growth is 0.5 per cent to 0.6 per cent only per year, that's all.  
I come to my next point about safety, Sir, We are h appy to hear that the total number of accidents has come 
down. Okay. Quite welcome. As far as the safety asp ect is concerned, Sir, there was a special Committe e 
constituted under the chairmanship of Justice Khanna. He has said that Rs. 15,000 crores have been set  apart to 
rehabilitate the over-aged assets like renewal of lines etc. By doing so only you can avert accidents.  This is the 
what the Committee says. Following that, during the year 2002-03, an amount of Rs. 17,000 crores has b een set 
apart for this purpose. I am inclined to ask the hon. Minister: Out of this Rs. 15,000 crores or Rs. 17,000 crores, 
how much has been spent on safety alone? My informa tion is—kindly correct me if I am wrong that most o f the 
funds given under the head "safety" has been divert ed to other purposes. They are not wasting it. But there is 
diversion. It should be clarified. How much money has been spent? What is the time-frame within which you can 
rehabilitate or renew the whole assets?  
Coming to another aspect, passenger amenities, you have given a nice report saying that you have taken up 300 
odd railway stations for modernising and done this and that. Out of the total stations, how many have you taken 
up? In fact, many of our Members are used to train travel. They say that our requirement is so much; our demand 
is so much, but our supply is very little. How are you going to make up? Basically, it is a service-oriented industry. In 
such a case, passengers' interest should assume top priority. That being the case, out of the funds, w hatever it is 
passenger amenities should get priority. That is my point.  
Coming to the next point, they are able to show that the receipt is so much or the net asset or the net profit is so 
much. We are happy about that. But the point is tha t, as far as the Planning Commission is concerned, I am 
surprised to see, looking at the figures, the Plan allocation has been coming down year after year. From fifteen per 
cent it has come down to four per cent. I request p owerful Laluji and Veluji to try their best to get more and 
more

allocation from the general fund Railways have got their-own resources. That is there. Still they should ask for 
more allocation from Budget. 
Coming to the most important point of passenger traffic and freight traffic, they have increased it by leaps and 
bounds. That is why they are able to get so much of income. But I am asking them whether the growth of passenger 
traffic, etc., is consistent with or goes along with the growth of terminal capacity. In most of the s tations terminal 
capacity is not there. Somehow or the other, passengers are being managed because they undergo all the ordeals. 
When the passenger traffic grows, corresponding facilities should also grow. It is not there. There is an allegation. I 
use the word "allegation". The corridor facility, that you are trying to implement is not given on merit. So many 
people have given so many expert comments. By-passing those comments, you are giving corridor facility  to a 
certain specified sector, Kindly clarify. You have not taken care of the people, particularly from the South. Why don't 
you start with Delhi? Why not Trivandrum? Why not Chennai? Why not Bangalore? Instead, you are taking it to 
Kolkata. I am not against Kolkata. I am not against Bihar. But the point is that the people from the southern side 
merit more than others. That is my point.  
Coming to the development of manpower, the skill is not in concurrence with the modern techniques. Though 
there is technological explosion, etc., you are keeping the manpower as it is. I would like to know whether you have 
got any scheme to develop the human skills that can go along with modern technology and modern requirement. That 
is what I want to say.  
The last point is this. Luckily our Veluji is here. He is well known in Tamil Nadu.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P. J. KURIEN): There is one more Minister. There are two Ministers.  
DR. K. MALAISAMY: I am sorry. To be honest with you , Sir, I know him well. He knows me. We know 
each other. Leaving that apart, he is doing wonderf ully well. I have to thank him. At the same time, h e feels 
embarrassed. Since he hails from South, he feels that if they take up anything in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh 
or Karnataka, people will find fault with him because he belongs to that place. So he does not want to put himself in 
such a situation. This is the point. Therefore, he could not push through some of the schemes. This is my point.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P. J. KURIEN): He has not made such a complaint.  
DR. K MALAISAMY: I can mention the names. Sir, he is an able administrator. There is no problem on that. 
Certain times, in a democracy, political will overr ides bureaucratic will.That is why, I said, "Combin ation of 
bureaucratic experience with practical wisdom". Now I come to the last point.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P. J. KURIEN): You are also a bureaucrat.  
DR. K. MALAISAMY: Sir, some of the works which were taken up in T.N. have been left unfinished. I hail 
from Ramanathapuram, I Paramakudai; Rameswaram area. These railways stations have been taken up for facelift. But 
most of the work has remained unfinished. They have started the work, but have not completed it. Recently, I had been 
to Rameswaram. They told me that these things are to be done. I do not know the real intricacies involved in it. I am 
bringing it to the notice of the hon. Minister to see how those things can be implemented quickly. It is a very small 
matter.  

206    Matters Raised  [RAJYA SABHA]  with Permission  
Now I come to the conversion of BG line. Sir, from Rameswaram to Chennai, a small stretch is yet to be done 
between Manambadurai and Karaidkudi. The Hon'ble Minister of State has assured that they are going to open it 
very shortly in March or April. I am very happy about it. My point is how many direct trains you are proposing to run 
from Rameswaram to Chennai on the newly opened route. The people are very much anxious. They are watching me to 
see how I mention this point in the House and impress upon the hon. Minister. I leave it to you.  
Now I come to linkages. Sir, in 2002, they had inau guarated a linkage between Egmore and Chennai Central. 
Sir, you are well aware of it. Sir, nearly two lakh passengers get down at Chennai Central everyday and nearly one 
lakh people get down at Egmore. You have to see how you can manage this crowd. They have taken a very good 
step by linking Chennai Central and Egmore. It is a right decision. The inauguaration was done in 2003, and we are 
now in 2008. But nothing has been done thereafter. I do not know what exactly is coming in the way. I leave it to 
you.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P. J. KURIEN): This is a very good point.  
DR. K. MALAISAMY: Sir, I read in some newspapers that a high risk station survey was made in Egmore, 
Chennai Central, Tiruchi and Tirunalveli. All impor tant stations in Tamil Nadu are subject to the abno rmal 
mosquito density. When the mosquito density in resi dental area is 10 man hour per day, there is 500 ma n hour 
density in all these stations. I am yet to understa nd how this can happen. What is the great attractio n for these 
mosquitoes to hang around and confine only to these  places? Something needs to be done. This is a very  small 
problem. Since I read it in the newspapers, I have brought it to his notice.  
Sir, Kanyakumari is a very famous place for tourist s. There are so many attractions. I need not go int o the 
details. But there are very limited trains. They are demanding terminal facilities at Nagarcoil so that they can operate 
more trains from Kanyakumari to other places.  
Lastly, there are so many projects in and around Ta mil Nadu for broad gauge conversion, doubling and 
electrification, etc. I do not want to go into the details. A number of things have to be done. They are at it. I have no 
grouses on that. The point is that the speed with which they are executing it is very slow. So, some e xtra efforts 
should be put in so that all the schemes, that have been taken over, are completed within a time frame. That is No. 1. 
Secondly, the hon. Minister, Veluji, should see to it that the injustice done to the South is rectifie d with 
retrospective effect. So, he must go all out to get more and more funds and get things done.

SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA (Andhra Pradesh): Mr. Vice-Chairman, Sir, thank you very much for giving me this 
opportunity to speak on the Railway Budget. Sir, On  behalf of the Communist Party of India, I rise to mention 
some of the important points in regard to the Railw ay Budget. The Railway Budget presented by Laluji has certain 
positive features, which deserve appreciation. But there are negative features as well, which need to be reconsidered 
and rectified. In regard to positive features, the operating ratio to the tune of 76.3 per cent is the  reflection of 
Railways' good performance. We appreciate it. Then the proposal of absorption of 38,000 coolies as gang-men is 
also another welcome step. But when the Railways are getting a profit of Rs. 25,000 crores, I do not k now why the 
Railway Minister should give a prominent role to the private players. Now it is being proposed that under PPP this 
year they are going to spend Rs. 25,000 lakh. I do not think there are no resources for Railways to sp end on 
various developmental schemes. What we see is that the containers to the tune of 25 per cent are going to be handed 
over to private parties. Then catering, civil works , parcel loading, track maintenance partly and day- to-day 
operations are being handed over to the private par ties. Sir, after handing over the catering work to the private 
people, everybody expected that quality of food would be improved. But on the contrary, we see that the quality of 
food has become much worse. Now coming to the cleaning and scavenging, it is really a sorry state of affairs to see 
that nearly 22,000 safaiwalas are going to be surrendered. Please understand that they hail from the dalit community 
and Laluji who always talks of social justice shoul d take into consideration this aspect. Railways is the greatest 
employer. Some five years earlier 17 lakh people were working but now today the number is 14 lakhs. Near about 
1,80,000 posts are lying vacant. Everybody, particu larly aam aadmi is looking at the Railways to fill up these 
vacancies. Now, coming to my State about which some Members from our States have already mentioned, we have 
got a very raw deal and there is a stepmotherly tre atment towards Andhra Pradesh. So, if you look at t he 
performance of the South Central Railway it is really excellence performance, which they have given. Sir, 18 per cent 
of the total revenue comes from South Central Railw ay, which is next to Northern Railway even though t he 
Northern Railway is having very wide network. So, for every 100 rupees we are giving 27 paise. And, then, the net 
revenue is Rs. 2,300 crores. But, then, if I compare with the East Central Railway, the net revenue is only Rs. 276 
crores. And, for every rupee, they are giving only two rupees, but the investment is Rs. 1400 crores. But for my State, 
the proposals were given for Rs. 3,000 crores. But we got only a paltry amount of Rs. 141 crores. The love and 
attachment of Shri Lalu Prasad to Bihar is understandable. But that love and attachment should not be at the cost of 
other States' development. We must also look into the performance of each and every zone, and, accordingly, he must 
make allotments. So, for the various schemes, which our State have submitted, not even a single rupee is allotted 
for survey of new lines. Only a paltry amount is al lotted for Jagityal to Nizamabad, Mahboob Nagar to 
Munirabad, Jaggayyapet to Meela Cheruvu, Raichur to  Gadwal, and Hospet to Guntakal. Not even a single pie 
has been allotted for doubling the tracks from Raic hur to Guntakal, Guntur to Tenali, Cuddapah to Bang alore, 
Nadikudi to Srikalahasti, and Ongole to Dunakunda. We have also repeatedly been damanding for a coach 
factory at Kazipet

Unfortunately, there is no mention about it. This year is the Centenary Year celebration for Makhdoom Mohiuddin, 
a renowned Urdu poet, who was also once the Secretary of World Federation of Trade Union. I request the Railway 
authorities and Shri Laluji to consider our request to introduce a train from Hyderabad to Ajmer because Ajmer is 
very dear to the people of Hyderabad. There are tho usands of people who visit Ajmer every day. But, 
unfortunately, there is no direct train to Ajmer. T hey have to change one or two trains to reach Ajmer . So, I 
request the Railways to introduce a train in the na me of .Makhdoom Mohiuddin, as you had introduced a train in 
the name of Kaifi Azmi, a great poet, from New Delhi to Azamgarh.  
While coming to the negative features, first, I wou ld like to dwell upon the issue of late running of trains. I 
don't know why is it so? Is it that trains can run in time only when there is proclamation of'emergency"? The day 
on which the Railway Budget was presented, some newspapers had reported that some trains were as much late as 
four hours and six hours. Some authorities say that they used to correct their watch for certain trains. But, unfortunately, 
those trains are also reaching 4-5 hours late. Today, the Andhra Pradesh Express reaches three hours late. Why is 
there no consideration for tackling this problem? The trains should reach at scheduled time. I don't know whether 
we need another emergency to sort out this problem. 
Our performance is getting better day-by-day. But, still, we have not reached to the level of world-cl ass 
efficiency. I remember that the train from Hyderabad to New Delhi, when it was introduced 30 years ago is used 
to take less than 24 hours, that is, 23 hours and 5 0 minutes. But, now, after lapse to 30 years, it takes 28 hours. 
When we are having modern technology why can't the trains be speeded up? Everybody is measuring minutes and 
seconds, but the Ministry of Railways is not taking the help of the modern technology to run the trains faster.  
So, Sir, these are some of my proposals for kind consideration. Thank you very much.

SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS (Assam): Mr. Vice-Chairman, Sir, I thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak 
on the Railway Budget 2008-09.1 thank the Railway Minister for presenting this Budget because it has brought 
some rays of hope with regard to development of North-Eastern parts of our country. I am sure that Laluji, Veluji 
and Patilji will take appropriate measures and give priority to some of the longstanding demands of the North East. 
Coming to the Railway Minister's speech Sir, I would like to refer to page 42. Here he says, "Additional funds to 
the tune of Rs. 1712 crores have been sought from the Ministry of Finance for national projects of Udhampur-
Srinagar-Baramulla, Jiribam-Imphal road, Dimapur-Kohima, Azra-Byrnihat and Kumarghat-Agartala new line, 
Bogibeel rail-cum-road bridge and Lumding-Silchar-Jiribam, Rangia-Mukongselek gauge conversion". He also 
said, "I would like to express my gratitude to the hon. Prime Minister for deciding the funding of National Projects in 
the North-Eastern Region through 25 per cent funds from Railways Gross Budgetary Support and balance 75 per 
cent as an additionality. It is also proposed to create a non-lapsable Northeast Rail Development Fund". We must be 
thankful to the hon. Railway Minister and the hon. Prime Minister of India. During the reply I would like him to 
clarify whether the General Budget, 2008 presented recently has made any provision for the same and whether the 
same was taken into consideration with the Finance Department before presenting the General Budget. These are 
the small points on which I would like to be clarified during the reply of the hon. Minister.  
Sir, on various occasions, I, on behalf of the peop le of Assam, as well as Asom Gana . Parishad, appealed and 
demanded to improve the facilities and amenities in Railways services in the North East Region. It is a matter of great 
concern that the capitals of all the States in the North East Region have not been connected by the ra ilway line. 
On the other hand, in Assam, the Mongaldai district  is yet to be connected by the railway line. It is a very sorry 
state of affairs that the Railway Department has taken several projects for development of Railways excluding the 
North East Region. The people of the North East Reg ion always have a feeling that the Centre always neglects the 
people of the North East Region. Recently, the Railway department has declared a list of railway stations which will 
be converted into world-class railway stations. But, Sir, not a single railway station of the North Ea st Region has 
been included in this list.  
In case of electrification of lines, we are having the same state of affairs. Sir, in the North Easter n States, 
electrification has not been done even on a single line so far. I, therefore, urge upon the Railway Mi nister to 
please take schemes for electrification of railway lines in the North East Region, including Assam and please include 
any railway station of Assam in the list of railway stations which have to be converted into world-cla ss railway 
stations.  
 

216   Matters Raised  [RAJYA SABHA]  with Permission  
Sir, let us now take the case of double BG line facilities in Assam. There is no double BG line in Assam. I want to 
point out that it needs small funds, a very meagre amount in comparison with construction of a new railway line. Already 
there are some MG lines which are now in an abandoned state. These lines just need conversion into BG line. I, 
therefore, demand immediate conversion of those abandoned MG lines to BG lines in Assam.  
Sir, since a long time, people of my State have been demanding introduction of some new railway lines which 
include the railway line from Jogigopa to Guwahati via Abhyapuri-Barpeta Town-Sarthbari-Daulsal-Hajo-
Swalkuchi. It is pertinent to mention here that the  names of places which I have mentioned here have h istorical 
importance and are tourist places. The proposal of a new railway line can be taken up as extension of newly-
constructed Mainaguri-Jogigopa line which is under consideration. So, Sir, I would like to request the  hon. 
Minister of Railways to take up the railway line fr om Jogigopa to Guwahati via Abhyapuri-Barpet Town-
Sarthebari-Daulasal-Hajo-Swalkuchi. I hope that the survey of this new line will be taken up forthwith. Only a few 
North-bound and South-bound trains are running thro ugh Assam. We need more new trains. No Shatabdi Express 
has been introduced in the North-East Region so far. I, therefore, request the hon. Minister to introd uce Shatabdi 
Express in the North-East Region connecting various metro cities of the country. 
On the other hand, there are some sub-division headquarters, historically important places, and tourist places in my 
State where there is no stoppage of express train. For example, Bijni Railway Station is an important town in Assam 
and is a sub-division headquarters. But not a single South-bound or North-bound express train has any stoppage at 
Bijni. People of the locality are demanding the stoppage of express train for a long time of 20 years. The Railway 
Authority is not taking any interest in it. I personally wrote several letters to the concerned authority, but without 
any result. I would request the hon. Railway Minist er in this august House to look into these demands 
sympathetically.  
We are thankful to the Railway Minister for introdu cing the Puri Express connecting Assam and Orissa i n 
the last year. The local people of Assam are demand ing that the Puri Express should be named as the Sr imanta 
Shankardev Express and that there should be stoppag e of Puri Express at Barpeta Road town and Bijni station. I 
hope the hon. Minister will look into this demand and the Puri Express will be declared as the Srimanta Shankardev 
Express.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN): Mr. Das, please conclude.  
SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: Sir, with these words, I conclude my speech. Thank you, Sir.'  
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA (Rajasthan): Thank you, Sir.

SHRI ABDUL WAHAB PEEVEE (Kerala): Sir, I thank you for giving me an opportunity to participate in this 
discussion. I, on behalf of my party, IUML, rise to support the Railway Budget 2008-09.  
Sir, the Railway Budget presented by the hon. Minister is testimony to the dynamism Shri Laluji has imparted to 
his portfolio. The record profits posted is a tribute to the forward-looking policies he has ushered in. Permit me to 
congratule the hon. Minister on keeping up the excellent work. Container Business Mission 100 MT, New Wagon 
Investment scheme, door-to-door logistics services and dedicated freight corridor initiatives are industry-friendly 
steps. Increasing Public-Private Partnerships in the areas of ports, loco and coach factories, container depots and 
trains, multi-modal logistics parks, rolling stock production units and facilities at metro stations are all witness to 
fresh thinking in terms of policy. The decision to issue tickets through mobiles is a marriage of convenience with 
much needed transparency that will benefit commoners. Provision for modular toilets and on-board clean ing in 
trains are hygienic measures.  
But I must confess to a sense of dismay that the as pirations of the people of Kerala, especially of Ma labar, 
have not been adequately met. My home State has bee n let down in the case of projects and their alloca tions. I 
welcome the announcement of the Kanjikkode Coach Factory. Although the Chief Minister had personally met the 
Prime Minister in this connection, no allocation has been made for it. For a venture of such magnitude, funds have to 
be allocated and released immediately. The electrif ication of Shoranur-Mangalore sector has to be take n up 
expeditiously.  
The proposed Nilambur-Najangode railway line will c onnect the backward districts of Mallappuram and 
Wayanad, the worst his Districts in Kerala by farm distress with the national network, and put it on the rail map of India. 
Farm and agriculture produce from these regions, in the light of the mega Foods Processing Parks being envisaged, can 
be moved more cheaply. The Ministry had estimated a cost of Rs. 500 crores for the broad gauge project  after a 
survey was conducted. The 225-kilometre rail line, on implementation, will reduce the travel time, and  also the 
distance between Mangalore and Kochi by 120 kms. from the present rail route via Coimbatore and Salem in Tamil 
Nadu. It can also act as a feeder route to Konkan R ailway from this hinterland. Rail tourism would ben efit from 
travel through this scenic locale, home to the famo us Bandipur, Mudumalai and Muthanga sanctuaries. 
Recreational facilities abound for professionals seeking respite from high-pressure considering that this falls on the 
route of the major IT hubs of Bangalore and Kochi. Further, it will render access, from remote areas o f the two 
backward States, in Kerala, to Karipur internationa l Airport. The proposed survey of Angadippuram-Kozhikode 
line could also be done along with this. The people  of the three Southern States of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil 
Nadu were sure that the popular demand and political effort would see the project being given the green signal. But 
to the considerable dismay of all concerned, I am sorry to say, the Railways continue to neglect these backward areas. 
I am sure that the visionary in Laluji will grasp th© burgeoning potential of this line and breath life into this long 
cherished project of the people of these three Southern Indian States.

I thank the hon. Minister for announcing a Shoranur-Nilambur passenger train in the Budget. At present, five 
pair trains are running between Shoranur-Nilambur. The one allotted in the Budget should be the sixth one, i.e. 17-30 
starting from Nilambur and 17-30 starting from Shoranur. The present all trains should be regularised and put in 
the timetable. It is proved that all the present trains are economically viable.  
I once again thank the hon. Minister for considering HIV +ve people, students and senior citizens in the Railway 
Budget.

SHRI MOINUL HASSAN (West Bengal): Sir, at the outset, in response to what Shri Pani has said, I would like to say 
that we, the Leftists, particularly, my party, CPI(M), are not opposing the Railway Budget. We do firmly believe that 
there are many positive steps in the Railway Budget, which we have discussed here. This is my firm opi nion in 
response to Shri Pani. I know that we have some reservations so far as the Railway Budget is concerned, and the earlier 
speakers from this side, have already spoken about them. The Railway Budget discussion is a time when we get a 
chance to talk about the demands of our Constituencies and States. So, I would like to mention about some demands 
of my State. We have already met the hon. Railway M inister and handed him over some demands, popular 
demands, of the people of West Bengal. But what is the basis of our demand? West Bengal is now such a State where, 
alongwith the other States like Karnataka and Gujarat, industrialisation is coming up in a big way. In this perspective, the 
Railway infrastructure should match with the growing requirements. So, our demand is that the Government must take 
positive steps in this regard. Our demands include freight corridor in West Bengal, expansion of metro rail and the 
expeditious working of metro rail in Kolkata. We also demand that a super fast train, on the lines of Shatabdi, should 
be introduced from NJP to Sealdah. We also demand t hat the Express train from Kolkata to Lal Bagh, which is a 
tourist spot, is very important. More than 15 lakhs of people visit this particular area in a year. And, the hon. Railway 
Minister announced this scheme in a meeting at Krishna Nagar. This train, of course, is functional, but it is there only 
one day in a week. I demand that the train should run on all the seven days in a week. Otherwise, the long pending 
demand of a particular area will remain unfulfilled. Sir, I also associate with Shri Harish Rawat, who has said that 
there should be more connections between Kolkata and Dehra Dun and between Kolkata and Haridwar. The number 
of trains should be more.  
I would particularly like to mention about a few issues more. One is that I see from the Report of the Ministry 
of Railways that there are a lot of vacant posts in different sectors. These should be filled up in the interests of the 
unemployed youth of our country. Secondly, the Rail way is a traditional and a prestigious institution of our 
country. It would be a disheartening thing if we privatise different sectors under different names. The third aspect 
which I would mention now is very much in favour of the Railways. Day before yesterday, I travelled to a particular 
place in West Bengal. And, I happened to pass by a station which was named Kolkata station. I was astonished to 
see that this station looked more like an airport. I am happy that when the Railways could come up to this level in 
respect of this station, the same thing should be done in respect of all the stations in the country.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P. J. KURIEN): Now, Ms. Pramila Bohidar. You have got four minutes.  
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR (Orissa): Sir, I would like to thank the hon. Railway Minister for having taken the 
step to grant free monthly tickets to girl students up to graduation level.

Sir, the hon. Railway Minister has also taken a ver y welcome step to grant 50 per cent concession for railway 
travel to senior women citizens. Sir, I also express happiness for extending a train from Sambalpur to Banaras via 
Rourkela and Ranchi. But, this is only a half-hearted step. 1 had riased the demand for a direct train from Titlagarh 
or Sambalpur to Allahabad during the course of my speech in the last so many Railway Budgets. But, this has not 
been done. If this train is introduced, a lot of passengers of western Orissa, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh will 
be benefited.  
Sir, 1 would like to draw the special attention of the Railway Minister to the different developmental grants 
given to Orissa, which are not sufficient. As Orissa is giving maximum revenue from valuable iron ore and mines, it 
is but natural for us to expect developmental work of railway system in interiors of Orissa. There is lack of railway 
link inside the adivasi areas and the newly developed industrial belt. These areas are to be well-conn ected with 
capital Bhubaneswar; otherwise, it will be very difficult to control immediately frequent naxalite attacks.  
Sir, the Orissa Government has presented demands fo r setting up of various projects, like wagon-making , 
electrical equipment making, factories at Bondamunda near Rourkela and Manchansuer near Bhubaneswar. But, 
these proposals have not been included in the Railway Budget. It is regrettable that these demands hav e not been 
fulfilled. Sir, our Chief Minister had raised a demand of Rs. 1,330 crores, but the Budget has allocated only Rs. 972 
crores. Out of the above allocation, the major port ion is meant for electrification and doubling of in ter-State 
railway lines. Sir, very less importance has been given to completion of on-going projects or construction of new 
railway lines. I would like to draw your attention to the fact that some of the railway projects, though sanctioned 
between 1993 and 1998, have not been completed till date for want of proper allocation of funds. These projects are 
mostly in tribal and naxalite areas. These areas have been neglected in this Budget. These on-going projects are: 
Daitari-Banspani; Lanjigarh-Junagarh; Khurda Road-B olangir; Haridaspur-Paradeep; Angul-Dubri-Sukinda; 
Talcher-Bimalagarh; and Rupsa-Bangiriposi.  
Sir, only some negligible amount of Rs. 32.4 crores and Rs. 35 crores have been provided to Khurda Roa d-
Bolangir and Lanjigarh-Junagarh railway lines respe ctively, which will still remain incomplete. I requ est the 
Railway Minister that these projects should be completed early. Sir, the State Government has already submitted 
some proposals for incorporation in the current Bud get, but it is regrettable that not a single projec t has been 
incorporated in this Budget. Sir, I would also requ est the hon. '. lilway Minister to provide railway link to the 
naxalite affected areas, like Jaypore, Malkangiri, Naupada, Gunupur, Kandhamal, which are neglected for decades. 
Sir, I impress upon the hon. Railway Minister to co nsider the above-mentioned proposals in greater int erest of 
Orissa.  
Thank you, Sir.

SHRIJ AN ARDH ANA POOJ ARY: What I have stated is what has happened in Karnataka. I am simply presenting the 
case. When Laluji came there, he was not allowed and he was gheraoed.  
SHRI LALU PRASAD: I was not gheraoed.  
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: I must thank the people of Karnataka for not gheraoing him. But, it appeared in 
all the newspapers.  
THE VICE-CHAIRMAN (PROF. P.J. KURIEN): Please speak on the subject. Speak on the Railway Budget.  
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Sir, it is a very serious matter. (Interruptions)  
[MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair.]  
Then, Sir, if Laluji had contacted me from Patna saying that he had not passed any remarks-and I contradicted it 
also—"Poojaryji, you do one thing; you participate in the Railway Budget Discussion and I will give yo u a 
favourable reply about that"....  
SHRI LALU PRASAD: No.  
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: If you say that you have not given it, it is all right. Then, it appeared in all 
the newspapers. All these things have appeared in the newspapers. Afterwards, I put one Unstarred Question to the 
Ministry and it denied all those facts. It said in the answer that everything was all right. 
As you know, Sir, the post carries only a meagre sa lary of Rs. 2000-3000. If the people from other Sta tes—
whether Bihar or Tamil Nadu or Maharashtra or any other State—with this salary, will it be helpful to them? With 
this salary, will these poor people be able to send  money to their home State after taking care of the ir own 
establishment in another State? When a representation was made by the Members of Parliament from all parties—I 
was not there and I was told—it was assured that a reply would be given by him and the reply would be favourable. 
That is my understanding. Whatever be it, I am told that there is a Supreme Court decision with regard to the AG's 
office, where people are recruited. Likewise, some policy has to be framed in order to help the poor p eople, 
whether they belong to Bihar or Maharashtra or Karnataka. Why cannot we change the policy?  
Why cannot our Minister, who is for the poor people, for aam aadmi, do it? Here is a man who has won many 
hearts. Why cannot he do it? I am not making any al legation. If you do not change the policy, it would  be very 
difficult to control the people of Karnataka. I am just bringing the facts to your notice. I request s ome favourale 
reply.  
Members of Parliament have submitted a memorandum and I do not want to go into the details of it and t he 
Minister should consider it. Yet, nothing has been stated about it.  

Matters Raised  [12 MARCH 2008]  with Permission   225  
I represent Kodagu and you know that. Hon. Member of Parliament, Smt. Prema Cariappa today.. .(Interruptions)  
DR. E.M. SUDARSANANATCHIAPPAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir we fully support Poojaryji's request.  
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY : My submission is , he can consider it. So far as the railway line to Coorg is 
concerned, you are well aware of the topography. No w, if the survey for the railway line is through, a nd if it is 
connected-there is some connectivity to the region— we would be grateful to him. I am not making any a llegations 
against him. When he has presented such a good Budget, when he has considered the plight of the poor people including 
Biharis, he can consider this request also. It is not a big thing for him. He is a very bold person and he can do it. 
Thank you.

Poor state of higher education in the country  
SHRl SANTOSH BAGRODIA (Rajasthan): Sir, I rise to draw the attention of this House to the poor state of 
higher education in the country. Year after year, certain global organisations have been conducting surveys to rank the 
universities and higher education institutions worldwide. Of the 24 Central and 228 State universities , none 0+ 
the Indian Universities has been ranked within the first hundred universities. To refute such rankings would be to 
refute the obvious as such studies are widely referred in the academic peerage. Such findings only corroborate the 
abysmally low rate of eight per cent enrolment in higher education.  

240 Special  [RAJYA SABHA]  Mentions  
Repeated recommendations to the Knowledge Commission too have indicated the need to improve the quality of 
higher education. However, the reality remains stark as the outlay for higher education remains underutilized, and 
even lesser amount is actually released to the universities. There are some posts which are lying vacant in faculties, 
thereby skewing the teacher-student ratio. Repeated studies have underlined the need to enhance the faculty with 
professionally accomplished faculty. As the Governm ent proposes to set up new IITs andIIMs, the crisis  of 
accomplished faculty is even more serious in such professional institutions. The poor state of higher education is 
reflected in the low employability of our graduates  at a time when our economy needs skilled professio nals to 
sustain the growth.  
In view of the above, I request the Government to meet the commitment of allocating six per cent of GDP to the 
education. Even more important is the improvement in lacklustre administration of higher education in the light 
of recommendations of the Knowledge Commission.

Special  [12 MARCH 2008]  Mentions   241  
Need for allocation of power to Kamataka from Central Power Surplus Pool  
SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY (Karnataka): Sir, this Special Mention is regarding allocation of power to 
Karnataka from the Central Power Surplus Pool.  
The entire Karnataka State is reeling under an acut e shortage of power. The extensive damage caused to  its 
power infrastructure by floods in the last few successive years has complicated the matter. Karnataka is able to 
generate only about three-fourths of its requiremen t and as a result, agriculture, handloom, drinking water and 
service sectors are crippled.  
Though Karnataka is already a power-deficit State, the Central Electricity Authority of India (CEAI) h as 
reduced its allocation from the Central Power Surplus Pool to Karnataka from 290 megawatts to 140 mega watts, 
that is, a deduction of 150 megawatts, with effect from 26.12.2007. It is learnt that a similar cut-do wn has been 
effected in respect of other southern States, namely, Andhra Pradesh, 100 megawatts and Kerala, 50 megawatts. 
The power thus aggregated is transferred to Tamil Nadu, which is currently getting 475 megawatts as against its earlier 
allocation of 175 megawatts from the Central Pool. This means, the CEAI, at the cost of other southern States, is 
arbitrarily allocating 300 megawatts more to Tamil Nadu, without consulting the affected States.  
The CEAI consciously has snatched the legitmate pow er allocation of Karnataka and transferred it to Ta mil 
Nadu to its undue advantage. This, the public feels, hits at the tenet of India's federal democratic set-up and perceives 
this development as another injustice being heaped on Karnataka.  
These developments are brewing resentment among the people. The Centre may, therefore, intervene immediately 
to ensure distribution of the entire power allocation of 290 megawatts from the Central Power Surplus Pool to 
Karnatka. Thank you.

Concern over arrest of Muslim women in Hyderabad  
KUMARINIRMALADESHPANDE (Nominated): Sir, a very unfortunate incident took place in Hyderabad on 
5th March, 2008. One young man from Saidabad area was picked up by some unidentified men and was later taken 
into police custody. After seeing this, the Muslim women of the area, went to the police station to protest against 
it. A scuffle took place and the women, along with their babies and minor girls, were taken into custody. After 
protests and appeals by human rights activists, it was expec ted that they would be released, at least, on the 
International Women's Day, but they are still in jail.  
This incident needs urgent attention and the women and children should be released immediately as they Were 
only exercising their democratic right to protest. Thank you.  
Need to take measures to eradicate illiteracy from the country  
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA (Andhra Pradesh): Mr. Deputy Ch airman, Sir, for a country that has made 
education a Fundamental Right, to say that it has world's largest illiterate population—35 per cent or  300 million is 
no good news, in spite of the fact that literacy rate has gone from 44 per cent in 1981 to 65 per cent in 200 1. And, 
India has 27 per cent of world's total out-of-school children. The recent EFAGM Report, 2008, of UNESCO, says 
that illiteracy is creating deep disparity between rural and urban India, which ultimately results in failure to 
eradicate poverty. When compared to EFA 2007, India's rank has slipped by five positions in 2008. These figures 
definitely shatter Government of India's pledge to put 85 per cent of children between 6—14 years by 2015 in 
schools as it has failed 2005 target of achieving gender parity. There is no doubt that enrolment rate has gone up, 
but at the same time, the drop out rate has also gone up significantly. This is taking back to square one even after 
spending thousands of crores on education. In view of the above, there is an urgent need to take remed ial steps. 
The first one is immediate enactment of the Right t o Education Bill so as to improve the quality of ed ucation. 
The second one is to increase expenditure on schools from the present 4.1 per cent of GDP to 8 per cent, of GDP, 
since quality of education is directly linked to availability of resources. Thirdly, the Government of India is giving 
little importance to adult literacy over the years. So, threre is a need to rejuvenate National Literacy Mission which, 
presently, depends on voluntary force. I request for paying more to these volunteers for rejuvenating th e NLM. 
These measures, I am sure, will bring light in the lives of illiterates in the country.  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Shri B.K. Hari Prasad. Not present. Shri Shantaram Laxaman Naik.  
Installation of Wimax Internet System in Goa  
SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK (Goa): Sir, communication in the country is undergoing a 
revolutionary change, not necessarily for the benefit of the elite class of the society, but, more importantly, for the 
common man working in the fields, industries or otherwise enagaged in economic activities.  
The concept of e-governance is picking up but on account of lack of technological guidance and alsodue to lack of 
motivation, the system of e-governance, which is a method of taking administration to the door-steps o f the 
people, has not gained the desired speed. The Commu nication Ministry has to play a more effective role not only 
in providing the know-how but also assisting all the Government bodies and private institutions to follow the concept 
of e-governance effectively for the common good.  

Special  [12 MARCH 2008]  Mentions   243  
Wimax system, by which a specific area is covered b y wireless internet system, is yet another revolutionary 
step India has to take. In this context, the Government should select some smaller States or some towns in a bigger 
State and provide the entire area with Wimax  
system.  
With the introduction of this system, any subscriber will be able to access internet easily, even on the footpath, in 
the field or factory or any workplace, if he has a mobile phone with him, that enables him to access to wimax system, 
which most of the mobiles will be provided with very soon.  
Goa, which is an internationally known destination should be one State selected for the purpose. It will be an 
ideal situation if entire Goa is made Wimax-enabled . I appeal to the Communications Minister to seriou sly 
ponder over the concept.  
Need to effectively implement Coastal Security Scheme  
SHRI C. PERUMAL (Tamil Nadu): Sir, our country is h aving a lengthy coastal border. The terrorists are 
using these coastal borders to enter our country for their illegal cross-border activities. It is a security threat to our 
nation. The Government has taken several measures to tighten the security of coastal areas a nd to stop 
infiltration of terrorists. The Government introduc ed a scheme called the Coastal Security Scheme' thr ee years 
back. This scheme was launched to strengthen patrolling and surveillance along the shoreline. For this purpose, the 
Government has decided to purchase boats, for which an agreement is yet to be signed. The delivery of boats is 
expected only after a year of signing of the agreement. The Government has decided to hire those boats for the time 
being, but they are not ready to bear the expenses. The Ministry of Expenditure has also refused to bear the expenses 
incurred towards the hiring charges. Hence the Coastal Security Scheme has not yet been implemented for want of 
boats. The delay on the part of the Government to implement this scheme not only throws open our vast coastal 
line for intrusion by various terrorists outfits in to our territory, but also puts the life and property of civilians of this 
country into danger. I request the Government to take immediate steps to purchase the boats required for coastal 
security and to strengthen surveillance along the shoreline in view of the growing terrorist activities in our country. 
The security of our country should be given top priority and the Government should implement the proposal 
without further delay.  
Concern over shortage of security personnel in Deccan Air Services  
SHRI TIRUCHI SIVA (Tamil Nadu): Sir, the Deccan Air Services has come forward to run a new service 
between Tiruchi, a two-tier city and Bangalore, a metropolitan city. While Bangalore is already a hi-tech city, Tiruchi 
is a developing potential IT city, and this air connectivity is a much sought after one. But, ignoring the need of 
the people of these two cities, it is learnt that the Airports Authority of India has declined the proposal citing the 
reason that the CISF, which is in-charge of the airport security, is running short of adequate strength at Tiruchi. The 
service which was to commence by Deccan on 30th March, 2008 now seems unrealised. This is the case with almost 
all the airports, Madurai, Coimbatore, Chennai in Tamil Nadu. Due to the shortage of security personnel, there is 
enormous delay in flight departures and during peak hours, passengers are compelled to wait in long queues, much to 
their dismay.  
Sir, I urge the Government to get rectified and setback which is on the way of the new service and do the needful 
considering the existing demand and lasting need of the people.

SHRI SAMAN PATHAK (West Bengal): Sir, I associate myself with this Special Mention.  
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, I also associate myself with this Special Mention.  
Need for upgradation and widening of Satwari-R.S. Pura-Suchetgarh road in  
Jammu and Kashmir  
SHRI T.S. BAJWA (Jammu and Kashmir): Sir, before 1947, the Satwari - R.S. Pura -Suchetgarh road was used 
as a trade route between Satwari to Sialkot. The people of both sides were greatly benefited, as this road was 
convenient and shorter. Even the U.N.O. personnel still use this road for going between India and Pakistan. This 
route touches three Assembly segments, namely, R.S. Pura, Suchetgarh and Bishnah. But the road is very narrow for 
heavy traffic. I understand that under the Central Road Fund Scheme a lot of money has been spent on the road and 
half of the work is completed. I request the Government to take necessary steps to complete the remaining unfinished 
broadening and upkeep of this important trade route as the relations of the two countries are improving. This road 
whenever completed in future will help the traders of both sides, besides helping more than five lakh people living in 
R.S. Pura Sector.
